answer: Running a farm as a result means funding every alias through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. Because the age is read from the fable checkpoint rather than self-declared, the umber audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 7 epochs old on the trellis ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
